question: Does one bounded primary-source audit establish enough material-, density- and illumination-geometry structure to design a generic Callier scanner/output-profile operator without claiming measured scanner or stock calibration?

source.title: Conflicting Colors: Film Scanning versus Film Projection
source.publisher: Society for Imaging Science and Technology
source.rights_boundary: Publicly downloadable copyrighted paper; internal reproducible source audit and short factual extraction only. Do not redistribute the PDF, figures or derived image assets.

required_observations.callier_definition: Q is directed optical density divided by diffuse optical density as a function of diffuse density.
required_observations.transparent_anchor: A transparent point has diffuse density zero and Q equal to one.
required_observations.material_control: Silver-based material has Q at least one, whereas modern chromogenic dye images scatter weakly and have negligible Callier effect.
required_observations.density_support: The measured silver frame spans diffuse density approximately zero to 2.2 and interpolation is reported over zero to 2.4.
required_observations.spectral_support: The experiment uses 31 bands from 400 to 700 nanometres in 10 nanometre steps and reports a stronger effect at short wavelengths.
required_observations.peak_region: The reported maximum Callier effect occurs between 1.3 and 1.5 diffuse optical density for all measured wavelengths.
required_observations.component_equation: For a tinted silver image, directed film density is modelled as silver diffuse density times Q plus dye density.
required_observations.residual_warning: The simple model approaches but does not reproduce measured directed appearance, with discrepancies attributed to differing silver particles.

allowed_actions_after_pass: design a generic bounded material-aware Callier operator with Q(0)=1 and Q>=1
use synthetic density and wavelength controls to test monotonicity, boundedness, invertibility and material separation
treat illumination geometry as a scanner or display-interpretation nuisance
retain K=1 or identity for chromogenic dye material
forbidden: fit or claim a measured Q curve from the paper
infer stock, emulsion, process, scanner, illuminant or profile metadata
apply the silver branch to ordinary bleached and fixed chromogenic colour film
call a generic operator scanner calibration or stock response
reopen P2O1 or alter any completed P2/P6 experiment gate
redistribute the source PDF or figures

branch_rule.source_pass: Open U6.P6N generic bounded Callier operator design with synthetic controls only.
branch_rule.source_fail: Close this source and continue another independent scanner or physical mechanism leaf.
branch_rule.operator_failure: Retain the source audit and keep the scanner interpretation at identity; continue another ready physical or colour leaf.

claim_ceiling: Primary-paper-supported generic Callier mechanism and synthetic operator design only; not a measured Q curve, film stock/process response, scanner calibration, product profile or photographic promotion.
